6.text: Women sometimes plait into their hair in front a number of small gay-

7.text: colored beads merely for ornament. In dressing the hair, the women form

8.text: two braids on the sides of the head, quite near the temples (Plate XXIX, Fig. 2).

9.text: The braids are adorned with strings of small beads and buttons (see Fig.

10.text: 188, g, h, k). Married women arrange their braids at the back of the head

11.text: in a coil, and cover them with a cotton neckerchief in Russian style (Plate

12.text: XXVII, Fig. 3). Young women and girls leave their braids hanging down over

13.text: the shoulders, and join their ends together with a narrow band.

14.text: The Chukchee allow the mustache and whiskers to grow. Only a few

15.text: young men pull them out with tweezers, which are probably copied after those

16.text: of some neighboring tribe. In this respect the Koryak are similar to the

17.text: Chukchee, while the Lamut and the Eskimo pull out the scanty growth of

18.text: hair on their faces very carefully.

19.text: TATTOOING. — Tattooing is done with a needle, by means of which a

20.text: thin thread, blackened with soot or with powder, is drawn through the skin.

21.text: It is practised on girls of ten years or even younger, though it requires con-

22.text: siderable endurance (see Plate XXX, Fig. 4). The women of the Reindeer Chuk-

23.text: chee are contented with only a few lines (Fig. 186, a). Two of these run

24.text: vertically on both sides of the nose. On account of these tattoo-lines several

25.text: tales speak of a heroine with a punctured nose as a Chukchee woman par

26.text: excellence. Several vertical lines adorn the chin. Childless women tattoo on

27.text: both cheeks three equidistant lines running all the way around. This is con-

28.text: sidered one of the charms against sterility. I know of cases, however, where

29.text: young women and girls have adorned their cheeks with such lines with no

30.text: reference to child-bearing. Many women of the Reindeer branch have no

32.text: Of the Maritime people, the Eskimo women, both on the mainland and

33.text: on St. Lawrence Island, adorn their faces and hands with more or less elaborate

35.text: The Chukchee of the Pacific villages south of Indian Point practise tat-

36.text: tooing similar to that of the Reindeer people, while in the northern villages

37.text: more elaborate designs are occasionally used (Fig. 186, f-h). In the Arctic

38.text: villages, so far as I am aware, the tattooing is like that of the Reindeer people.

39.text: Men are not tattooed, except in the Eskimo villages and the nearest

40.text: Chukchee settlements, where a great many have two small marks tattooed on

41.text: both cheeks near the mouth (Fig. 186, i). Nelson suggests that they may be

42.text: substitutes for labrets, which possibly were worn by the people in olden times.¹
